Abstract

The review summarizes recent evidence linking lactylation with tumor biology and therapeutic resistance.

Introduction

The introduction establishes the biological context and explains why the modification is clinically relevant.

Overview of lactylation

This section defines the modification and integrates evidence about writers, readers, and erasers.

Mechanisms of lactylation-mediated therapeutic resistance

Mechanistic evidence is organized across radiotherapy, chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy.

Strategies targeting lactylation to overcome tumor therapeutic resistance

Therapeutic strategies include limiting lactate production and modulating lactylation-associated enzymes.

Challenges in targeting lactylation

The review closes by distinguishing current limitations from testable translational opportunities.
